answer: At each reward pulse, an identity must burn independently verified compute credits worth $2 to qualify for at most $1 of subsidy; credits confer no voting rights. The quartz receipt registry rejects reused serials, so a plume of new keys still needs a separate burn for every seat. Even fully compliant clones lose money on the subsidy: each extra identity consumes more scarce compute than its capped payout returns, assuming credit verification cannot be forged.
